stories.title: Over 5,000 deaths reported in DRC’s deadliest Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: More than 5,000 people have died from the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to government data. The outbreak began in May and became the country’s deadliest in August, with a current case fatality rate of 48.6%. The epicenter remains in the conflict‑affected Ituri province, complicating response efforts.
stories.why: The high death toll and difficulty accessing the conflict zone increase regional health risks and strain international containment resources.

stories.title: 69 dead after high‑speed train collision south of Madrid
stories.summary: A collision on the high‑speed rail line south of Madrid left 69 bodies recovered from wreckage strewn across the tracks and down an embankment in central Spain. The disaster comes weeks before a snap general election called by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, adding pressure to his government.
stories.why: The incident could erode public confidence in the rail network and influence voter sentiment ahead of the election.

stories.title: Nvidia in talks to co‑sign debt for Nscale’s West Virginia AI data center
stories.summary: Nvidia is discussing a residual‑value guarantee that would back billions of dollars in debt financing for Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia. The arrangement would let Nscale secure funding for construction and electricity costs, with Nvidia stepping in if Nscale defaults, temporarily taking control of the facility and helping find a buyer or new tenant. Anthropic has a $44.6 billion contract for the first 460‑MW building, and a second deal of roughly $45 billion is being discussed.
stories.why: It illustrates Nvidia expanding its role from chip sales to directly underwriting AI‑infrastructure projects as investors grow wary of large‑scale build‑out spending.

stories.previousSummary: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday .
